title: <Application name> - <Side A> vs <Side B>
subtitle: Side-by-side review in plain language, from a senior mainframe developer's point of view  |  <D Month YYYY>
intro: What the application does in two sentences, who built each side and from what, what was compared (folders, file counts), that it was judged as a senior mainframe developer would before production sign-off, whether anything was compiled or run, and 'No customer data appears in this document.'
verdict: Headline fact one. One or two sentences.
Headline fact two. One or two sentences.
Which side is the better base and why.
Production readiness. Include the two averages from the scorecard (e.g. 3.4 vs 3.2).
same: Plain-language list of what is identical (layouts, tables, flow, error codes).
average_note: One line on where each side's strengths lie
differences: What each side does, why it matters in production, in 2-4 plain sentences. Tag must start with a side name (e.g. '<Side B> better'), or be 'Mixed' or 'Decide'.

sample_output.intro: Optional - delete this whole object when there is no sample trace. State the input assumptions and label derived/synthetic output as such.

shared: Problem both sides have. Plain-language explanation and what operations must do about it.
fix_intro: Neither package would pass a senior review as is. These are the items to fix before scheduling, most important first.
fix_a: Most important fix for <Side A> first.
fix_b: Most important fix for <Side B> first.
housekeeping: : duplicate, stray or stale files and docs.
glossary: The programming language the application is written in.
Instructions telling the mainframe what to run and in what order; a PROC is a reusable set of steps.
